items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen in walks of 10 to 19 minutes. In one program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Eating dinner at 8 pm or later is linked to a rise in sugar, with dinners at 8-9 pm linked to a rise about 13.3 mg/dL more than dinners before 6 pm. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see how it affects your sugar levels.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: A longer overnight fast may be linked to changes in sugar levels, with one program showing a change of -0.03 points compared to coaching alone. Your overnight fast averaged 10.0 hours, and you may want to try extending it to see how it affects your sugar levels.
